name: Minhoto Portuguese

allophone_rules.notes: Overridden for this northern variety: the nucleus is the close-mid [e], not the central [ɐ]. Matching it here, not disabling it, also keeps the stressed nucleus away from any tonic-[e] diphthongisation rule of the spec. Northern EP keeps the close-mid nucleus of word-final ⟨-em -ens⟩: [ẽj̃], [ẽj̃ʃ] (bem [ˈbẽj̃], homem [ˈɔmẽj̃], homens [ˈɔmẽj̃ʃ]). The centralised [ɐ̃j̃] of the pt-PT base is the Lisbon merger: Wikipedia 'Portuguese phonology', 'In Greater Lisbon, [ẽj̃] has merged with [ɐ̃j̃]'; Ciberdúvidas (Viana & Rocha 2006, 'Vogais e ditongos nasais, outra vez', n. 1): 'em dialectos do português europeu … a grafia -em/-en(s) representa o ditongo [ẽj̃]'. Leite de Vasconcellos 1901 (Esquisse d'une dialectologie portugaise, §44n, p. 93; quoted from an OCR copy, diacritics normalised): '-em < l. -ENE correspond -ẽ dans certains endroits de la frontière de Tras-os-Montes et du Minho, et -ẽi ou -ɐi dans le reste du pays'. The border monophthong [ẽ] is local and not modelled. The oral parallel in the same section (§44i): the diphthong ⟨ei⟩ is [ɐj] only 'à Lisbonne' and [ej] in Entre-Douro-e-Minho, the Beira and Trás-os-Montes. The rule matches ⟨m⟩ only, so word-final ⟨-en⟩ (hífen) is not matched here and falls to PT_FINAL_EN_NUCLEUS of pt-PT.
Overridden for this northern variety with PT_FINAL_EM_NUCLEUS: the nucleus of the plural ⟨-ens⟩ is the close-mid [e], so it is [ẽj̃ʃ]. The sources are under PT_FINAL_EM_NUCLEUS in this spec.

Restricted to POST-tonic syllables in the Minho. A pretonic ⟨en em⟩ before a consonant keeps the reduced vowel, nasalised: [ɨ̃] (pensar [pɨ̃ˈsaɾ], lembrar, pensamento, vender, tendência, entender [ẽtɨ̃ˈdeɾ]). Leite de Vasconcellos 1900 (Estudos de Philologia Mirandesa I, §76, p. 238): 'Este phenomeno é caracteristico da lingoagem do Alto- e Baixo-Minho; toda a gente culta d'estas regiões … diz usualmente lẹmbrar, tẹmporada, intẹndimento, pẹnsamento, vẹnder (ou mesmo bẹnder!), tẹndencia'; the ring below is 'e surdo (= ẹ) nasal' (p. 201, table b, 'Como na pronúncia do Minho, nas palavras pensar, tentar, lembrar'). He cites Dialectos interamnenses VI §3, IX §8-b and Gonçalves Vianna, Essai de phonétique, p. 46, n. A word-initial ⟨en em⟩ takes the base word_initial [e] and is not reduced. The post-tonic ⟨-em -ens⟩ still un-reduces, so homem stays [ˈɔmẽj̃].

notes: Minhoto Portuguese (Baixo-Minho: Braga, Guimarães, Vizela), a northern EP dialect in Cintra's Baixo-Minhoto-Duriense-Beirão group. MODELLED FEATURES: (1) APICO-ALVEOLAR-ONLY SIBILANT SYSTEM — the archaic four-sibilant opposition is reduced to a single apical branch: graphemes ⟨s⟩/⟨ss⟩ AND ⟨c⟩(before e/i)/⟨ç⟩/⟨z⟩ all realise as apico-alveolar [s̺] (voiceless) / [z̺] (voiced), unlike the conservative four-sibilant Transmontano/Alto-Minhoto system which keeps apical ⟨s/ss⟩=[s̺] distinct from laminal ⟨c/ç/z⟩=[s] (Cintra 1971 p.93; Álvarez Pérez 2014 pp.37-38: this group 'kept only the apico-alveolar branch'). Coda ⟨s/z⟩ keep the pan-EP chiado neutralisation to [ʃ]/[ʒ]. (2) BETACISM — the /v/–/b/ opposition is neutralised to /b/, realised as stop [b] or spirant [β] (Cintra 1971 p.88; Pérez 2014 pp.35-37, categorical in the far north). Porto's tonic close-vowel diphthongisation ([e]>[je], [o]>[wo]) is a Baixo-Minho/Douro-Litoral subdivision trait and is NOT applied here (kept to pt-PT-x-porto). Vowel-reduction and uvular-coda allophones are enumerated as northern variants. Inherits pt-PT base. ⟨ss⟩ is declared apico-alveolar [s̺] here because the pt-PT base maps it to plain [s]; the value follows feature (1) above, which puts ⟨s/ss⟩ in the apical branch. Cintra 1971 (read in the Instituto Camões CVC reprint, pp. 11-13) draws the main North/South isogloss on the sibilant of the graphemes s and ss: apico-alveolar in the North, predorsodental in the South. His southern limit of the apical runs from the Ria de Aveiro to the Mondego, which it crosses upstream of Coimbra, and on towards Castelo Branco.

ancestors.notes: Standard European Portuguese; Minhoto diverges mainly in vowel reduction and uvular coda realization

sources.notes: Foundational EP dialect classification. p.93: the Baixo-Minhoto-Duriense-Beirao group reduces the archaic four-sibilant system to two apico-alveolar sibilants [s̺ z̺]; p.88: /v/-/b/ merger and apico-alveolar sibilants are diagnostic northern features.

sources.author: Álvarez Pérez, Xosé Afonso
sources.title: European Portuguese dialectal features: a comparison with Cintra's proposal
sources.notes: ALEPG-corpus quantitative reassessment. pp.37-38: Baixo-Minhotos, Durienses and Beirões 'kept only the apico-alveolar branch' (both s/ss and c/ç/z merge to apical), vs the conservative four-sibilant Transmontano/Alto-Minhoto. pp.35-37: /b/-/v/ merger extends along the coast beyond Coimbra and through the eastern districts (Guarda, Castelo Branco).

stress.notes: Acordo Ortográfico 1990 conventions: paroxytone default; written accents override; final -i/-u/-r/-l/-z/-x/-im/-om/-um/-ins/-ons/-uns and nasal diphthongs attract final stress. Unmarked -em/-ens/-am stay paroxytone (homem, homens, falam): an oxytone of more than one syllable in -em or -ens is written with an acute (Acordo Ortográfico 1990, Base VIII, 1.º c: deténs, haréns, provéns, também). DIPHTHONGS: declared so the bundled syllabifier counts nuclei correctly — without them every vowel run merges into one nucleus and co-e-lho is read as coe-lho, one syllable short, putting the stress and its vowel reduction on the wrong vowel. ⟨oe⟩ is hiatus, not a diphthong (Cunha & Cintra, §Ditongos). COMPOUNDS: a hyphenated compound is one prosodic word. Each element keeps its own stress and the last is the strongest (Bechara, Moderna Gramática Portuguesa, p. 340, quoted in Ciberdúvidas, resposta 28042), so compound_stress is "last": guarda-chuva gwˌaɾdɐˈʃuvɐ (Portal da Língua Portuguesa). IPA_DIPHTHONGS is empty: the grapheme table writes every diphthong with a glide ([aj], [uj], [ɐ̃w̃]), so two full vowels side by side in the transcription are always a hiatus, and the stress mark is placed with each IPA vowel as a nucleus of its own. Read with the orthographic list, the IPA [ui] of ⟨proíbe⟩ /pɾuibɨ/ and [iu] of ⟨viúva⟩ merge into one syllable and the mark lands a syllable early. The acute on a tonic ⟨i u⟩ after a vowel marks exactly this hiatus (Acordo Ortográfico 1990, Base X, 1.º: juízes, ruína, ciúme, miúdo, saída, baú).

location.notes: the historical Minho province — the Baixo-Minho zone (Braga, Guimarães, Vizela) the variety covers. [Wikidata Q512317 P625]

clup_dialect.measured: The clup_dialect row holds 9 scored sentences (clup_dialect is sentence-level: each gold entry is one interview sentence, scored as a single unit against the engine's whole-sentence transcription, so the bootstrap resamples across only 9 sentence-level PER values, not across words), per=0.3181, per_ci_low=0.2908, per_ci_high=0.3471 (benchmarks/results.json). At n=9 sentences the bootstrap interval is already collapsing toward a point for the same reason (few distinct values to resample), so its narrow width reflects the small sample, not precision; see docs/scoreboard.md's `95% CI` note and the THIN_ROW_MARK cutoff (rows under 20 scored items). This row cannot gate a production promotion on its own strength.
